page.layout: One printed page (right), with a running head at top and page number at top right. Main text in one column: a continuing line, a paragraph with Greek, a tree diagram with braces, a section heading, a numbered theorem with two paragraphs, then a signature and catchword at the foot. No marginal notes on this page. The left strip shows the gutter edge of the facing page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: est, numeri, quo minorem duo pluresue exacte diuidere nequeunt.

Euclidi est Ἐ λάχις© ὑπὸ τινῶν μετρέμεν©. Dati enim quotlibet numeri plures composítos ut facere, ita quoq; diuidere possunt, è quibus minimum deligere, numerandi dexteritati facilitatiq; plurimum confert.
main_text.l: Quorum autem minimus communis diuiduus quaeritur, uel sunt
Bini tantum, ἴἴ͵ aut inter se
Plures, ubi minimus diuiduus occurrit uel
main_text.head: Inuentio minimi à datis communiter diuidui ex sequentibus Theorematibus est.
main_text.p: Si duo inter se primi dentur, factus ex ijs, est minimus à datis diuiduus. 36.p.7.
Vt datorum 3 & 5 inter se primorum minimus communis diuiduus est 15, factus ab utroq;. Item duorum 7 & 9, communis diuiduus minimus est 63.

page.notes: The left strip (fragments such as "maxi-", "in plu", "or inter") is the gutter edge of the facing page and is left out. The Greek in the paragraph beginning "Euclidi" and the Greek symbols in the diagram ("ἴἴ͵") are uncertain and are my best reading. The sign after "Bini tantum" may be a Greek numeral or abbreviation. The signature "D II." may be printed as "D ij." and the diagram's Greek characters were not fully legible.
